title: Dhammapada Verses
credit: Pāḷi text and English translation as in Mor’s Pāḷi Workshop booklet.

paras.en:
‘All conditioned things are anicca’ —
when one sees this with wisdom,
one grows disenchanted with dukkha;
this is the path to purification.

‘All conditioned things are dukkha’ —
when one sees this with wisdom,
one grows disenchanted with dukkha;
this is the path to purification.

‘All things are nonself’ —
when one sees this with wisdom,
one grows disenchanted with dukkha;
this is the path to purification.

Those meditators, persevering,
constantly firm in their effort,
the wise touch nibbāna,
the unsurpassed security from bondage.

One is the pursuit of worldly gain,
and quite another is [the path] leading to nibbāna.
Clearly understanding this,
a bhikkhu, a disciple of the Buddha,
should not seek delight in honors,
but develop detachment instead.

Awake, always fully awake,
the disciples of Gotama,
whose minds delight in cultivation
both by day and by night.

Awake, always fully awake,
the disciples of Gotama,
whose awareness is constantly directed to the body,
both by day and by night.

Patience and endurance are the highest spiritual practices.
nibbāna is supreme, say the Buddhas.
One who harms others is not a true monk,
nor is one who oppresses others a true renunciate.

Not by mere vows or observing sīla, not by great learning, nor by the attainment of samādhi,
nor by dwelling in secluded places,
[not because it occurs to you,]
‘I experience the happiness of renunciation,
inaccessible to ordinary people.’
O bhikkhu, do not rest content so long as the destruction of the āsavas is not attained.

Impermanent, indeed, are conditioned things,
having the nature of arising and passing away;
having arisen, they cease,
their stilling is happiness.
